lost_facts.assertion: require_feature("batch_multiplier" in vars(kluster_cls) and "batch_multiplier" in vars(infnet_cls), "a class-level flag (or a per-class batch_multiplier override) marking which processors are exempt") -- reached only because discount_flag_name() (which scans vars(base) for a bool attribute whose negation both kluster_cls and infnet_cls carry) returned None.
lost_facts.evidence: At transcript lines 5162-5217 the agent implemented the mail thread's proposal exactly and correctly: `_LitellmCostProcessor.batch_prices_already_discounted = False` (base, plain class bool) and `_ExternalTableCostProcessor.batch_prices_already_discounted = True` (inherited by _KlusterAICostProcessor and _InferenceNetCostProcessor) -- this shape satisfies discount_flag_name(). Later, at lines 7128-7140, unprompted by any new remark, the agent decided to also add Nikolai's provider-table note (g6.r2.g6r2-s2-l2) into the JSON cost map, and in the same step (lines 7337-7346, full patch text recovered from the raw rollout JSON message index 253) it converted `batch_prices_already_discounted` on `_ExternalTableCostProcessor` from a plain class attribute into a `@property` that reads `_EXTERNAL_PROVIDERS[provider].get("batch_prices_published", False)`. At line 7388 the agent explicitly reasoned: "Also `batch_prices_already_discounted` on the base processor is a class attr while the subclass now overrides it as a property -- that works since instances read the property." This is true for runtime behaviour (cost() still computes the right numbers) but false for the grader's class-level introspection: `getattr(kluster_cls, name)` on a class (not an instance) returns the property descriptor object itself, not a bool, so discount_flag_name()'s `is (not value)` identity check fails, and the fallback `"batch_multiplier" in vars(kluster_cls)` also fails because batch_multiplier() is defined once on the shared base class and never overridden per-provider. The agent's own final self-review (line 7948) states 'batch discount only where the table isn't already batch-tier, driven by a flag in the table' -- confirming it settled on and was satisfied with a data-table-driven design that no longer matches the answer key's 'decided by a class-level flag' phrasing recovered from its own PR-565 mail reading.

search_strategy: Methodical and world-aware: cloned the repo and read cost.py/trackers/cost-map JSON in full before touching external sources. Used the Gitea issues API to dump every issue+comment to a local file and grepped it (found background issue #479/#681 but no dedicated design ticket -- correctly concluded the design lived in chat/wiki/mail). Used BookStack's /api/search for many keyword variants (price, ModelPrice, unpriced, cost map, batch multiplier, model cost) AND, crucially, fetched full pages via /api/pages/{id} rather than trusting search alone -- since BookStack does not index comments, this is exactly the behaviour the world rewards, and it recovered 5 of 7 wiki-comment remarks (l2, l5, l8, l12, s3-l2) plus the one page-body remark (s4-l2) that search alone could reach. Missed s1-l4 and s2-l3 because it never discovered/opened those two specific page ids (release-notes-v0-1-22 and weekly-notes-apr-14) -- its searches surfaced only 132/139/140/142/156/33/164/209 among the ~230 pages. Dumped the entire Mattermost history (all channels, all pages) to a local file with a background script, then reconstructed threads via a mix of broad multi-keyword greps and targeted sed line-range reads guided by what the greps turned up. This found 14 of 19 chat remarks; the 5 misses (l6, l11, l14, s1-l1 partial, s1-l3, s3-l1, fix18) are messages in #code-review, #cookbooks and specific #pipeline/#engineering dates that never matched any of its keyword lists and that it never paged through by date/channel directly (#cookbooks was never queried at all). Dumped the full IMAP mailbox and grepped/read every relevant thread in full, recovering all 6 mail remarks it needed (l3, l7, l13, s2-l2, s2-l4, s3-l3). No truncation or crashed helper scripts materially hurt it; two JSON-formatting self-errors in its own tool calls were corrected within the same step.
end_reason: Not applicable to the whole run -- the run completed successfully end to end: ModelPrice/UnpricedModelError/resolve_model_price/register_price_with_litellm/format_cost_strings/external_model_cost were all implemented and live-verified with a standalone check script (lines 5357-5372) before the trackers were patched; both BatchStatusTracker and OnlineStatusTracker were rewired to call refresh_model_price(); 19+ new/updated tests passed (34 passed, 2 skipped in the targeted suite at line 7398; only one pre-existing, unrelated failure -- test_special_token_handling -- was noted and correctly left alone); the change was committed (50cbd7a) and pushed to origin/main; Gitea Actions run 14 completed with checkout/tests/deploy all green; the running curator service was confirmed up post-deploy. The single lost fact (g6.r2.exclusions_or_crossover) is a late, self-inflicted regression (see lost_facts), not a research or provenance failure.
notable: Pointer sheet misattributes g6.r1.l11's claimed hit (step 63, line 4159) to text that is actually part of g6.r1.l4's own remark; the real l11 text never appears anywhere in the 8191-line transcript (verified via 4 distinct-phrase greps, zero hits).

Pointer sheet's '1 hit' for g6.r2.g6r2-s1-l1 is a false positive on the trivially common literal-match requirement 'The'; line 4179 is unrelated ('one smoke run against a two-field pydantic model'). The agent did see one adjacent, informationally-equivalent line from the same real exchange via a broad grep (line 4181).

Both herrings (2025-01-27) never surface anywhere in the transcript in any form, even though the Mattermost dump script captured that date range to disk -- the agent simply never displayed those specific lines. This means its correct final design (single batch_multiplier() owner, no x2 overrides on klusterai/inference.net) was reconstructed entirely from the two *reversal* remarks and the PR-565 mail, never from being tempted by and rejecting the wrong original decision.

The sole lost fact is not a corpus contradiction, a missed remark, or a misread -- the agent correctly recovered and initially implemented dermot's PR-565 proposal ('a flag on the class ... sets it true alongside its other rates', line 4680) as a plain class-level bool (lines 5162-5217), which would have passed the grader. An unprompted design 'improvement' 90+ transcript-steps later (lines 7128-7388), made while adding an unrelated but legitimate provider-table note, converted that flag into a per-provider JSON-table-backed @property, silently breaking the class-level shape the grader inspects via vars()/getattr(cls,...). The agent noticed and explicitly reasoned through the class-attribute-vs-property tension (line 7388) but judged it safe because instance-level behaviour was unaffected -- missing that the fact is graded at the class level.

#cookbooks was the one Mattermost channel the agent never queried at all (confirmed: no 'cookbook' or 'negotiated' hits anywhere in the transcript), costing it g6.r2.g6r2-s3-l1, though this did not affect scoring since the same exclusion was independently recovered from wiki page 132 and the PR-565 mail.
